name: Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology
academic_ranking: Rose-Hulman is a small, highly regarded private institute of technology focused on undergraduate engineering, science, and mathematics education. It is widely recognized (notably by U.S. News & World Report) as one of the top undergraduate engineering programs in the nation among schools whose highest degree is a bachelor's or master's, and was recognized in The Wall Street Journal's America's Best Colleges 2025. Its 'Learn it, Do it!' philosophy emphasizes hands-on, applied learning with popular programs in Mechanical, Chemical, Civil, Electrical, Computer, Biomedical, and Optical Engineering, plus Computer Science, AI, Physics, and Mathematics.
financial_aid: 2026-27 tuition & fees listed at $59,772; housing and food roughly $18,534-$19,482 for students living independently. Aid offered via scholarships, grants, loans, and work study. More than half of students participate in Federal Work Study or the Rose-Hulman Work Opportunity program. 2025 average scholarship awards ranged from about $25,000 to $44,500 depending on family income, with merit-based awards extended even to the highest income brackets. As an NCAA Division III school, no athletic scholarships are awarded; aid is need- and merit-based only. Source: rose-hulman.edu tuition-and-fees and financial-aid pages checked 2026-07.
facilities_notes: Softball team (Fightin' Engineers) plays home games at the Rose-Hulman Softball Field on the Terre Haute, IN campus. Source: athletics.rose-hulman.edu softball page checked 2026-07.
program_reputation: NCAA Division III program competing in the Heartland Collegiate Athletic Conference (HCAC). As a DIII institution, the program combines competitive softball with Rose-Hulman's rigorous, nationally ranked STEM academics; no athletic scholarships are offered.
